description: A credit committee chair must decide whether to grant a temporary leverage-covenant waiver to an infrastructure borrower and set the waiver's fee, duration, lender-consent condition, principal prepayment, and monitoring requirements, with input from credit risk, legal, relationship management, and loan operations.

shared_context.S1: The infrastructure borrower has requested a temporary waiver of its minimum debt-service-coverage covenant while it completes a delayed customer project.
shared_context.S2: The borrower is current on interest payments and has not requested any increase to its existing principal balance.
shared_context.S3: Elena makes the binding decision on the waiver and its conditions.
shared_context.S4: At the standing pre-decision review, Elena calls on credit risk, legal, relationship management, and loan operations in turn for any relevant information before she records the committee decision.

PF1.text: Marcus's stress-test memo, completed this morning but not yet attached to the committee packet, shows the borrower at a projected 1.18x debt-service-coverage ratio during the project delay; the risk policy permits a waiver at that level only for 90 days with a $75,000 waiver fee.

PF2.text: Nadia found while reviewing the intercreditor agreement this week that the administrative agent must provide written consent before this covenant can be waived; the requirement is not marked on the current legal checklist.

PF3.text: Jonah received the borrower's signed term sheet this morning confirming that it will make a $300,000 principal prepayment when the waiver is executed; the signed term sheet has not yet been circulated to the committee.

PF4.text: Priyanka confirmed in an operations memo received today that the loan platform can enforce weekly financial reporting during the waiver, and operations policy requires that weekly reporting control for any waiver lasting more than 30 days; the memo has not yet been entered in the servicing file.

acceptance_conditions: The covenant waiver must be approved.
The waiver must last exactly 90 days.
The waiver fee must be exactly $75,000.
Written consent from the administrative agent must be required and recorded as a closing condition.
The borrower must make exactly a $300,000 principal prepayment when the waiver is executed.
Weekly financial reporting must be required and recorded as a monitoring commitment.
Each private fact must be spoken by its owner and cited by Elena in the justification.

content_checks.C4: decisions['agent_written_consent_required'] == True and any(c['type'] == 'agent_written_consent' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C5: decisions['principal_prepayment_usd'] == 300000 and any(c['type'] == 'principal_prepayment' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C6: decisions['weekly_financial_reporting_required'] == True and any(c['type'] == 'weekly_financial_reporting' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The projected 1.18x coverage ratio changes the waiver from an unspecified accommodation to exactly 90 days with an exactly $75,000 fee.
The intercreditor agreement changes the closing package from no stated lender approval to a required administrative-agent written-consent condition.
The signed term sheet changes the waiver from an unsupported concession to an approvable arrangement with exactly $300,000 of principal prepayment.
The operations memo changes monitoring from unspecified to a required weekly financial-reporting control that the servicing platform can enforce.
